title: The Tower That Would Not Integer
allegory: A mathematician climbs a tower of π, each level an exponentiation. At the fourth level, the air thins to a fractional mist — 0.31766... The tower refuses to land on an integer. The geometer measures the curvature of each rung, computes the intersection number, and whispers: "It was never meant to land."
commentary: Analytical fractional part: 0.3176613450. Intersection invariant: 0.2398. Monte Carlo bias noted. Tower manifold implemented in bytropix C. WuBu nesting maps right-associative tower to nested Poincaré spheres via Hamilton encoder.
footnotes: Schanuel's Conjecture implies transcendence, but we wanted the certificate ourselves.
Monte Carlo bias (0.456 vs 0.318) traced to Hopf sampling distribution — corrected in v2.
